Culture.name: {=XM9EPZDi}Satsuma
Culture.text: {=60nJZSa2}Satsuma occupied a unique position in the late Bakumatsu. The Shimazu lords maintained semi-independence, joining the shogunate under their own terms while remaining largely unconquerable. The domain was highly militarized, with a dense network of goshi samurai and a distinctive castle system. Satsuma's samurai were renowned for their loyalty, identifying first as Satsuma men, and the domain played a key role in supporting pro-imperial movements leading into the Meiji Era.{newline}{newline}Foreign Merchant: British

Culture.name: {=JSiAyodh}Mito
Culture.text: {=y6BfVZul}The people of Kanto, the spiritual homeland of the samurai class, live in a predominantly flat region that is perfect for extensive agriculture and the breeding of its renowned battle steeds, which yield abundant harvests and allow Kanto to field and maintain cavalry forces more easily. Imbued with the secular martial tradition in which they have their roots, the lords of Kanto can more easily raise large armies to face their enemies, but their great emphasis on military preparedness makes it more expensive to pay the wages of their soldiers.{newline}{newline}Foreign Merchant: Dutch
